# Rondo · European football analytics

Open-data analytics for men's European football: a possession-value model with player ratings and match reports, and a recruitment tool that finds players by style and physical profile.

**Status: in progress.** Phase 0 (setup) is under review. No results yet. Every number this README shows later will be generated by code from the data.

> Independent project by Moulik Jain. Not affiliated with any data provider, league, federation or club.

## What it will do

- **Value:** a possession-value model, player ratings, next-morning match reports and a coach app.
- **Scout:** "find players like X", with style and physical profiles.

Both sit on one tested data foundation built from StatsBomb and Wyscout event data and open tracking data. GPU-trained models ship only when they beat strong CPU baselines on pre-registered tests.

## Data credits

- [Event and 360 data: StatsBomb open data.](https://github.com/statsbomb/open-data) The StatsBomb logo will appear here, as StatsBomb's terms require (pending).
- [Event data: Wyscout open data (Pappalardo et al., 2019, Scientific Data 6:236), CC BY 4.0, converted and aggregated by Rondo.](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4415000.v5)
- [Tracking and event data: DFL open data (Bassek, Rein, Weber & Memmert, 2025, Scientific Data 12:195), CC BY 4.0, converted and aggregated by Rondo.](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.28196177.v1)
- [Player identity and birth dates used for the minors rule: Wikidata (CC0).](https://www.wikidata.org)
- [Licence for the CC BY 4.0 datasets above.](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Full terms, citations and how Rondo follows them: [docs/DATA_TERMS.md](docs/DATA_TERMS.md).

Rondo is non-commercial. Its code is MIT-licensed ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). That licence doesn't cover provider data or outputs derived from StatsBomb data, which may not be used commercially.

## Running it

Needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node.js (version in `web/.nvmrc`).

```bash
make setup      # Python 3.12 env (uv, locked) + web dependencies
make lint test  # ruff + pytest
make web-build  # static site into web/dist/
```

`make help` lists every target.
